correctness.rationale: For H^1 and D^1, T(t) is a C0 affine composition semigroup with norm at most C exp(t), uniformly in t; the commuting binomial expansion bounds the spectral radius by R. For any nonzero |lambda|<R, strict triangle geometry selects a simple zero of a phase-perturbed exponential sum at Re s<1. Irrational Kronecker torus density plus Rouche produces infinitely many distinct exact zeros of F(s)-lambda in Re s<1. Independent analytic powers (1-z)^(-s) are H^1 and D^1 eigenfunctions, so lambda is non-Fredholm on both preduals. Closedness fills zero and circle; predual similarity and Banach duality transfer spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum. No finite experiment or unchecked numerical lemma is used.

value.rationale: The 2026 focal paper motivates determining full and Fredholm essential spectra under weak boundedness assumptions. A naturally simplest unsupported class is a two-atom positive measure. Incommensurability changes the Fredholm spectral geometry from possible polynomial images to an entire disk and gives infinite predual eigenspace multiplicity for each nonzero interior point. The arithmetic phase effect is a structural, sharp, reproducible infinite-dimensional spectral phenomenon, not a routine numerical example or arbitrary slice.
